title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 72–73): Grothendieck is building the 'déploiement' (unfolding) of a stratified space X. The space is filtered by closed unions of strata X_i indexed by a poset I. The goal is to replace X by a family of manifolds with boundary or corners, glued along their faces.

- For each stratum i, Σ_i is the closed stratum X_i with the open 'standard' tubular neighbourhood of the lower strata removed (eq. 92). It is a compact 'core' of the open stratum.
- For i<j, Σ_ij is the boundary of a tubular neighbourhood of Σ_i inside X_j, with the singular part coming from the intermediate strata (i<k<j) cut out again (eq. 93). Σ_ij is the total space of the 'link bundle' of stratum i in stratum j, a face of Σ_j. Grothendieck's sketch on p. 72 shows a link drawn as a circle around a point, with three segments leaving the point.

This page first states the desired outcome. One wants Σ_ij ⊂ Σ_j, provided the choices defining Σ_i and Σ_j are made coherently. More generally, for i<j<h, the faces Σ_ih and Σ_jh of Σ_h should be in correct relative position. Their intersection should then be the corner piece Σ_ijh. So the Σ's indexed by chains i_0<...<i_k of I should form a manifold with corners whose faces are indexed by chains of the poset.

To make the choices coherently, Grothendieck proceeds as follows.
1. He introduces a strictly increasing 'dimension function' δ : I → N. Its role is to linearise the induction, playing the part of a depth or dimension function.
2. He forms the increasing filtration by closed sets X_(d) = ∪_{δ(i)≤d} X_i (eq. 44), with X_(-1)=∅ ⊂ X_(0) ⊂ ... ⊂ X_(N)=X, where N = sup δ (eq. 45).
3. He builds by induction a decreasing filtration by closed sets X^(0)=X ⊃ X^(1) ⊃ ... ⊃ X^(N+1)=∅ with X^(d) ⊂ X \ X_(d-1) (eqs. 46–47).
4. A crossed-out sketch makes the recipe explicit:
   - T_0 is a standard tubular neighbourhood of X_(0).
   - X^(1) = X minus the open neighbourhood T̊_0.
   - T_1 is a standard tubular neighbourhood of X_(1) minus T̊_0, taken inside X^(1).
   - X^(2) = X^(1) minus T̊_1, and so on.

This is the familiar inductive construction of a coherent system of tubular neighbourhoods, in the spirit of Thom–Mather control data. At each step one removes an open tube around the next skeleton within what is left. Then Σ_i is the trace of X_i on X^(δ(i)), and the boundary pieces satisfy the required incidences. The page stops at the set-up (the next page is missing).
errors: Eq. (47) is written X^(i) ⊂ X \ X_{i-1}. It should read X^(d) ⊂ X \ X_(d-1), with the parenthesised filtration index, as the 'i.e.' line itself shows. There is a similar index slip X_{-1} for X_(-1) in (45).

In the crossed-out sketch, 'X^(1) = X \ X̊_(0)' should be X \ T̊_0, i.e. the complement of the open tubular neighbourhood. Otherwise X^(1) would not be closed, nor contained in X \ X_(0) as (47) requires.

Not an error but a gap: the coherence claims (Σ_ij ⊂ Σ_j; Σ_ih ∩ Σ_jh = Σ_ijh) are only asserted heuristically. The page breaks off before the inductive step that realises them; the 'suffisamment petit' conditions are not made precise.

ideas.what: Unfolding (déploiement) of a stratified space into compact manifolds with corners Σ_{i0...ik} indexed by chains of the stratification poset, with Σ_ij ⊂ Σ_j and Σ_ih ∩ Σ_jh = Σ_ijh.
ideas.modern_name: Resolution / unfolding of Thom–Mather stratified spaces into manifolds with corners with iterated fibration structure ('unzipping').
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5–6: announced 'théorème de déploiement' in tame topology; no proof given there.

ideas.what: Strictly increasing dimension function δ: I → N, used to linearise the induction over the poset of strata, with the closed filtration X_(d) = ∪_{δ(i)≤d} X_i.
ideas.modern_name: Depth/dimension filtration (skeleta) of a stratified space.

ideas.what: Inductive construction of a decreasing filtration X^(d) by removing open standard tubular neighbourhoods of successive skeleta, so that X^(d) ⊂ X \ X_(d-1).
ideas.modern_name: Inductive construction of control data / compatible system of tubular neighbourhoods.

missed.claim: The coherence of choices making the Σ's indexed by chains of I fit together as faces and corners is set up but not carried out on this page. The proof sketch for the déploiement theorem announced in the Esquisse remains unpublished. The result itself is now established by others (Verona; ALMP; Ayala–Francis–Tanaka).
missed.quote: Pour ajuster ces choix, de façon à avoir, pour i<j<h, des Σ_ih et Σ_jh dans Σ_h en position relative correcte
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mainly historical: it documents how Grothendieck intended to prove his announced déploiement theorem. The method is essentially Mather's, so there is little new mathematics.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine set-up page for the inductive Thom–Mather style construction behind the déploiement theorem announced in the Esquisse. The chain-indexed corner structure Σ_ijh is a nice glimpse of Grothendieck's intended picture. However, it is now standard (ALMP, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka), and the page contains no completed new result.
transcription_corrections: '(47) X^(i) ⊂ X \ X_{i-1}' should be read as X^(d) ⊂ X \ X_(d-1); the 'i.e.' line confirms the parenthesised index.

In the crossed-out sketch: 'X^(1) = X \ X̊_(0)' — the image has 'X^(1) = X \ X̊_(0)', but the intended meaning is X \ T̊_0. The line '[-...-] X^(1)' at the end of the T_1 line is likely 'X^(1) ∩ T_0' / a crossed-out fragment.
'leur intersection soit le voisinage[?] des Σ_ijh' — the word is uncertain; the intended sense is that Σ_ih ∩ Σ_jh is (the union of) the corner pieces Σ_ijh, not a 'voisinage'.
'(comme on le [-en donnant plus haut-])' likely reads '(comme on l'a fait plus haut)' with crossed-out continuation.
Top-right margin: 'à condition d'avoir ajusté de façon cohérente les choix qui donnent Σ_i, Σ_j' — consistent with the image.
